title: Detecting Arbitrary Order Beneficial Feature Interactions for Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Recommender systems need to detect beneficial feature interactions, including higher-order interactions.

gap.claim: Examining all possible higher-order interactions is exponentially costly, so existing approaches detect only limited orders and may miss beneficial interactions beyond those limits.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes HIRS, a hypergraph neural network model for generating beneficial feature interactions of arbitrary orders and using them for recommendation prediction.
The method uses three properties of beneficial feature interactions and deep-infomax-based methods to guide interaction generation.
The number of generated interactions can be specified below the number of all possible interactions to reduce running time.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that HIRS is the first work to directly generate beneficial feature interactions of arbitrary orders and make recommendation predictions accordingly.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that HIRS outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms by up to 5% in recommendation accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Beneficial feature interaction detection is important for recommender systems.
Exhaustively examining higher-order interactions is prohibitively expensive.
Existing methods therefore limit interaction order and may miss higher-order benefits.
HIRS uses a hypergraph neural network, arbitrary-order interaction generation, interaction-count control, and deep-infomax-based guidance.
The authors report up to a 5% recommendation-accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art algorithms.

source_observation.claim: Exhaustive enumeration of higher-order feature interactions grows exponentially with interaction order.

interpretation.claim: A useful interaction-discovery strategy should avoid searching the full combinatorial space.

application.claim: In recommender systems, generate a smaller, selected set of candidate interactions while allowing arbitrary interaction orders.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the reduced interaction set preserves recommendation quality or which interaction orders are most useful.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the three properties used to guide interaction generation.
The abstract does not specify datasets, baselines, experimental settings, or absolute accuracy values.
The abstract does not quantify running-time reductions.
